compress

/kum-PRESS/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Compress means to press or squeeze something together so that it takes up less space.

The machine at the recycling plant can compress hundreds of aluminum cans into a single dense cube.

Worked Example

Before the hike, Dana had to compress her bulky sleeping bag into a stuff sack the size of a loaf of bread.

Compress fits because Dana is squeezing the sleeping bag together, forcing all its loft into a much smaller space.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

compact: To compact something is to pack it down tightly so it holds together — machines compact trash, snow compacts underfoot. Compress is broader: it covers any pressing into less space, gentle or forceful, and extends to shrinking digital files. Compacting packs material solid; compressing simply forces it smaller.

condense: To condense something is to make it denser, shorter, or more concentrated, and it is the usual word for shrinking words and ideas — you condense a chapter into a summary. Compress is the physical counterpart: you compress air, springs, and luggage by squeezing them into less space.

cram: To cram is to stuff things forcibly into a space that barely holds them — cramming clothes into a suitcase. Compress reduces the thing itself, forcing it to take up less room; cram just jams items into a tight container, leaving each item the same size as before.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

expand: spread out; become larger

inflate: fill with air; swell up

Where it sits · how violently it is forced smaller — squeeze → compress → crush

squeeze vs. compress: You can squeeze a sponge gently with one hand; to compress it is to force it fully into a smaller space.

crush vs. compress: Compressing something packs it tighter but leaves it whole; crushing it destroys its shape completely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — com-

Prefix — com-: Latin, 'together, with'

Root — press

Root — press: from Latin pressare/premere, 'to press, push against'

Put it together

Put it together: Com- ('together') plus the Latin root press- ('to press') builds the word's meaning directly: to press together. What you compress ends up denser and smaller than it was.

Use the root in a new word: suppress

Use the root in a new word: suppress: She had to suppress a laugh during the solemn ceremony — pressing it down before it could escape.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / technical

Compress is the go-to word for physically squeezing things into less space — air, springs, trash, luggage — and it has a common digital sense too: you compress a file to make it smaller to store or send. For shrinking words or ideas rather than objects, English usually prefers condense.
